discovery: Invention and development of the optical lattice atomic clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock: neutral atoms confined in an optical lattice at a 'magic' wavelength where the trap does not perturb the clock transition. This combines the long interrogation of a trapped ion with the signal-to-noise of thousands of atoms. Katori's group demonstrated the concept, and Ye's group pushed it to extraordinary performance, reaching systematic uncertainties and stabilities in the 10^-18 to 10^-19 range, orders of magnitude beyond cesium standards. They used ultrastable lasers and interacting many-body systems of atoms. These clocks have resolved the gravitational redshift over a millimetre within a single atomic sample and made relativistic geodesy practical. They also set stringent limits on variations of fundamental constants and on dark matter. Lattice clocks are a new measurement paradigm, they are driving the redefinition of the SI second, and they have become a platform for probing fundamental physics.
